summary: Three findings: one high error in the retained compatible-root integral algebra, and two medium unresolved integration gaps concerning Div^1 properness/smoothness and mixed-characteristic affinoid period-ring reuse. The latter two revalidate prior confirmed area findings against the accepted round-three proposal. The fixed/relative split, integral special fibre, Proj-map correction, theorem conservation and proposed node-order repairs otherwise withstand the checks documented in the report.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-20.result.json layers[RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y].reason and RS-20.md node reconciliation; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y/chart-cover-perfectoidness-and-sheafiness proofSteps[2] in the integrated decomposition and partial RF0 packet.
findings.claim: The reconciliation fixes t_1^sharp to pi/[varpi] but leaves generators pi^(1/p^m)/[varpi] in the defining integral algebra, rather than compatible roots of the entire quotient. On the n=1 boundary |pi|=|[varpi]|=c<1 these generators have norm c^(1/p^m-1)>1 for m>0, so cannot lie in the asserted A^+. Their p-th powers also fail the displayed root-coherence relation. Keeping that algebra builds the wrong integral object even after correcting the reciprocal.
findings.evidence: Fargues-Scholze, Geometrization, author-hosted 356-page PDF, proof of II.1.1, printed p.48, https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/Geometrization.pdf (read 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-01; SHA-256 9ab9efbd0df251bfa3b610d1d1d88a8dfb1bdf7c397bd04f4c277280d98ae905): the displayed tower is '(pi/[varpi])^(1/p^infty)', with roots on the whole quotient. The inherited expression instead roots only pi. Its own following relation pi^(1/p^m)=[varpi]^(1/p^m)t_1^(1/p^m) agrees with the source tower, not its preceding algebra definition. The report gives independent valuation and p-power computations.
findings.fix: Extend the accepted reconciliation instruction to correct proofSteps[2] as well as the reciprocal: adjoin pi^(1/p^m)/[varpi]^(1/p^m) compatibly for every m, then take the stated [varpi]-adic completion. Carry both corrections into the RF0 packet, reader and suggested signatures through the authorized blueprint/fix workflow, without directly editing the reviewed base. Require root coherence, boundary boundedness and the reduction relation as separate acceptance checks. Preserve the integral pi=0 fibre and split-module sheafiness argument.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-20.result.json layers[RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts], owners and links; RS-20.md ledger for RF2:untilts/div1-moduli-and-properness.
findings.claim: The accepted keeps clause retains Div^1 properness and cohomological smoothness at the early untilt stage without supplying DiamondEtaleCohomology:C4 or DiamondSixOperations:S5 or naming a precise later property owner. Saying late properties need their own inputs does not route those inputs. This is the integration gap confirmed as RT-AREA-padic-1/17; its detailed late-stage fix proposal has not been incorporated into the accepted restructuring.
findings.evidence: Fargues-Scholze, Geometrization, Proposition II.1.21 and proof, printed p.56, same URL/version as /1: properness follows 'from the valuative criterion [Sch17a, Proposition 18.3]' and the smoothness proof invokes Proposition 24.5. C4 owns ECD section 18; S5 owns the Spd Q_p example 24.5 and the necessary coefficient cases. Neither is an ancestor of RF2:untilts in the fresh assembly. The inherited node explicitly names both inputs. The partial RF0 packet requests S4, not the missing S5 example. The prior /17 review confirms the same missing ancestry.
findings.fix: Split the moduli definition from the property theorem in the restructuring and authorized blueprint. Assign the latter to a late RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:div1-properness stage, or an equally precise existing later owner, with RF2:untilts, C4 and S5 inputs and the finite-extension/equal-characteristic argument. For the named child include RF2 -> RF2:div1-properness so aggregate inference cannot reverse its dependency. Forward to HS0 and VS1 and any other evidenced consumer; keep early divisor/period-ring inputs to RF3, RF4, VB1 and BG0. Move rather than delete the property proof. Coordinate with RT-AREA-padic-1/17 to fix this once.

findings.claim: The proposal names Mathlib's carriers and integral-divisor completion but does not import R06.1's mixed-characteristic affinoid period-ring/filtration plan. The matching p-typical generic specialization therefore still lacks an explicit theorem-reuse boundary. The accepted R06.1 node already works over a characteristic-zero perfectoid K and its perfectoid affinoid algebras, not only C_p. This is the scoped gap in confirmed RT-AREA-padic-1/20 and RT-AREA-padic-2/21, not a claim that all-E integral period geometry duplicates arithmetic Hodge theory.
findings.evidence: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, author PDF dated November 3, 2012, Section 6 pp.35-36, Lemma 6.3 and Corollary 6.4, https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/pAdicHodgeTheory.pdf (read 2026-10-01), includes 'any perfectoid affinoid (K, K+)-algebra (R, R+)'; its construction and filtration are already in the accepted R06.1 node. FS VI.2, printed pp.196-197, identifies the geometric-point completion with the usual O_E-relative de Rham ring while retaining a characteristic-p Witt specialization. Mathlib Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 defines BDeRhamPlus by completion and BDeRham by localization at images of theta-kernel generators; its carriers vanish for p=0 in the input. Naming those carriers does not route R06.1's theorem obligations. There is no R06.1 -> RF2:untilts path.
findings.fix: Add an explicit R06.1 -> RF2:untilts comparison/import for the matching mixed-characteristic p-typical affinoid case, reflected in suppliedBy, ownership, node prerequisites/request and reader. Reuse the existing general-K affinoid filtration plan after identifying the completion, residue map and generator; do not reprove it locally or unnecessarily generalize a C_p-only statement. Retain RF2's all-E coefficient comparison, arbitrary-base descent, integral/equal-characteristic constructions, geometric DVR comparison where not yet supplied, and possibly nontrivial graded line bundles. Prove coefficient-change compatibility before extending reuse. Coordinate with the prior confirmed area findings.
